findings.title: Machine V4 may run before author pass 1, and the author who runs it sees its codes
findings.problem: Draft 6 lets V4 code 'any time after item 3', so V4 can run before item 4 (author pass 1). The author is V4's operator. Section 9 V4 requires the author to inspect every conversation for tool use, and `collect` stores and prints each answer. So V4's codes can reach the author before pass 1 is committed. No file seals V4's codes from the author. A17 and R8 seal only the pre-codes, and V6 covers only what V4 sees. Pass 1 is then not blind to the coder whose agreement with it gates every design-limit claim (line 430) and Step 4(b) eligibility (line 480). Draft 5 ordered V4 after pass 1 without saying so, because pass 1 selected V4's cases. Draft 6 dropped that selection, and nothing replaced the ordering. C2's due date, seven days after the pages and sub-cause list are frozen, leaves room for pre-coding, 10–18 h of pass 1 and 4–8 h of V4, so in practice it pushes V4 to run during pass 1. 3b inherits the same order (line 305: 'following items 3, 4, 5 (all cases), 7 and 8').

findings.title: The known-answer set counts 17 records, but under the case unit it holds only 11 cases, so 'at least 14' cannot be met
findings.problem: The amendment defines a case as one value in one run at each distinct loss step, taken at that step's earliest failing checkpoint (line 301). In the frozen 23-loss-trace.json, both strict and lenient, the A0 records lost at state maintenance with bug3_replaced_in_own_meeting number 17 value×checkpoint records. They collapse to 11 cases over 10 values: 144b6dec F29 (k=1,2,3) and F68 (k=2,3); 48405ba5 F21 (2,3), F50 (2,3), F61, F62, F81; 44a72348 F06 (2,3), F58, F62, F66. If the page builder makes one page per case, the gate needs 14 of 11, so V4 always fails and the fallback skips Step 4(b). If it makes one page per record, the 'cases' are not cases, and the repeats of one value (F29 three times) are scored as independent passes. The rule can be applied two ways. Also: (a) the expected answer is taken from the flag, not checked against line 378's earlier-boundary rule ('When two boundaries would each have prevented the loss, the earlier is primary'). 15 of the 17 records are `overwritten_by_non_gold_value`, where a rival about another matter would put caused-at at routing under line 375. (b) The gate says 'caused at state maintenance', but the schema's caused_at value is "state rules". (c) No script or file picks out or scores the set.

findings.title: Voided answers cannot be recorded, re-asks are unbounded and unlogged, and the author decides voids after reading the answer
findings.problem: Section 9 V4 says that an answer showing other tool use 'is void and the packet is asked again'. The script cannot apply this. I tested it in scratch. Once a format-valid answer is collected, `collect` refuses any further attempt ('audit-08 already has a valid answer'), and it has no void flag. If the author voids before collecting, `stage` refuses to restage ('the workspace holds an answer that was not collected'). The only way out is to delete answer.json or a response file by hand, which leaves no record. When the agent writes no answer.json, for example because it replies in chat as the packet itself says ('Do not use tools. Return one JSON object and nothing else.', template:50), `collect` crashes with FileNotFoundError and records no attempt. The packet can then be restaged and re-asked any number of times, outside R7's two-attempt limit. `--response` also accepts a chat reply pasted by the author. Whether an answer is void ('reading or listing another path': does listing the workspace count?) is decided by the author after seeing it. That matters most for the 17 known-answer cases, whose expected code the author knows: a failing gate can be steered by voiding. The same path applies to every V4 case code that enters the kappa.

findings.title: Antigravity's agent is not confined to the workspace, and nothing records that it stayed there
findings.problem: V1 claims that staging means 'the agent can reach no other packet, no repository file, no git history and no memory file'. Staging controls only what the folder holds. The agent's terminal runs as the author's OS user, so it can read the repository on the same disk. The repository holds files that break blindness: 23-am1-audit-list.json (its roles determine every v1 label, per 23-am1-audit-list.py:76-80), 23-loss-trace-adjudications.yaml, 23-loss-trace.json (whose bug-3 flags give away the known-answer set), the committed pre-codes and pass 1, and, after item 4, any Step 2 output (line 411 keeps outputs hashed-only only 'until item 4 is committed'). The guards are the instruction text and a check the author makes afterwards. V2 lists settings that must be off (rules, saved knowledge, MCP) but gives no way to check or record them. The terminal or auto-execute policy is not fixed, so 'If Antigravity asks for approval' may never happen. The evidence is optional: exports are kept only 'where offered'. The pre-coder's channel audit (blindness check 4), which the template makes the gate for its channel (point 2), has no counterpart for V4. Section 9 replaces R1–R6 and R9 and adds none. An examiner cannot verify that any V4 answer was blind.

findings.title: V4's forced re-codes after the reveal (and 3b) have no instrument, and 'blind to the other's codes' is not workable for an author-run V4
findings.problem: Item 8 needs both coders to re-code cases whose boundary an oracle or leave-one-out moves, or whose row result differs between v1 and v2. These are the cases that decide line 480's agreement on caused-at and sub-cause. Section 9 and 23-am1-v4.py build only blind case packets and audit packets. Nothing says what a V4 re-code packet contains (the page plus which revealed outputs, in what wording), and nothing builds or checks one. The fixed prompt cannot carry revealed outputs: it tells the coder the sealed outputs exist and 'You will never see them'. So V4's re-code input would be written by the author after the reveal, with the results known: an instrument not fixed in advance, on the cases that matter most. 'Blind to the other's codes' can also hold only one way. The author has already seen V4's blind code for each case as its operator (L2-1), and no order is fixed between the author's and V4's re-codes, so the author may see V4's re-code before making their own. For 3b (line 305), the same gaps apply. V3's 'same model for every packet' cannot be met months later, and nothing says whether the known-answer gate is re-run if the Gemini model changed or what 3b's due date is.

findings.title: The leak checks do not formally cover V4's packets, and the audit packets carry a label-correlated cue
findings.problem: Section 6 and blindness checks 1–7 are written for the pre-coder's pages and prompts. For V4's case packets, Section 9 says only that check 3 'can' compare prompt hashes with the pre-coder's records. It is not required, and `case-packets` accepts any --pages folder. No check covers the audit packets at all. Their contexts are read from the run folders' *.state.json without any check against the run manifest. I ran audit-packets with salt TEST-review: 430 items, 8 packets, no role field, no grouping by role, ids are sha256(fact_id|text). There is one cue, though. The list is chosen by v1 label (all false decisions on extraction-lost values, only true carrier decisions on rows lost at filing or state maintenance), so how many items share a gold value within a packet tracks the label. Items whose value appears once in their packet are v1-true 62 of 123 times (50%); those whose value appears 5 or more times are v1-true 3 of 58 times (5%); the base rate is 134/430 (31%). The context count leans the same way (3 contexts: 33/72 true; 1 context: 78/284). B24, Section 9 and the docstring also say the packet holds fact_id, but the script prints none.

findings.title: The author runs V4 and may do so before pass 1, which breaks pass-1 blindness
findings.problem: Draft 5 selected V4's cases from pass 1, so V4 necessarily came after item 4. Draft 6 lets V4 run 'any time after item 3', and the author operates it. The author stages every packet, reads each conversation to check for tool use (V4 rule) and approves or declines tool actions. On an invalid answer, collect prints the problems, which can include quoted text and the sub-cause. So if V4 runs before pass 1 is committed, the author sees V4's codes for the same 180 cases before coding them 'blind'. A17 seals the pre-codes until pass 1 is committed for exactly this reason, because line 430 needs the author's codes made without them. Nothing seals V4's codes. There is also a timing conflict. The C2 due date counts from items 1-2, but V4 may start only after item 3 (pre-coding every case, with per-call audits). A slow item 3, or the fix below, can make the due date pass and trigger the fallback for reasons unrelated to V4.

findings.title: The known-answer key is not established and rewards the surfacing-step default that line 378 forbids
findings.problem: The 'known answer' is taken from a defect flag, and the trace's codebook calls such flags can't-tell markers. The bug-3 flag only records that a value was replaced by one with the same valid_from. The bug-3 repair stops only a lower-ranked rival, and the page shows no extraction confidence (the page code prints polarity and modality only), so the page cannot show that the loss rests on bug 3. Ten of the 11 cases are overwritten_by_non_gold_value, which the codebook reads as 'usually' wrong routing. The other, F06, is displaced by another gold value, F39. The case page (line 395; template 712) also shows the A1 runs, where bug 3 is repaired. At the same checkpoint, F06 is lost in all 3 A1 runs, 2 of them at current:displaced. F66 is lost at current:overwritten in 2 of 3. F29, F58, F61 and F81 are lost in 3 of 3, and F21, F50 and F68 in 2 of 3. A coder who applies E3/line 378 correctly can therefore code routing or unclear and fail the gate. A coder that defaults caused-at to the surfacing step and the class to implementation passes it. The set also exercises only E6 step 3 (Phase B bug), which the schema allows only for A0, so it says nothing about how V4 separates implementation from design on the 180 A1/A2 cases. It has no negative controls. No one has checked that the author or the pre-coder would score 14 or more.

findings.title: The script cannot void an answer, so it cannot apply the V4 rule that a void answer is asked again
findings.problem: Template V4 says an answer is void, and the packet is asked again, if the conversation shows any tool use other than reading packet.txt and writing answer.json, or if the author declined an approval prompt. Blindness check 5 also voids a record that declares "other" and has the case re-run. The script has no command or flag that records a void, and both routes to a re-ask fail. (1) If the void answer is well formed and was collected, collect refuses every later answer with "already has a valid answer". (2) If the author voids it before collecting, the uncollected answer.json blocks every later stage. The only way out is to delete files in responses/ or the workspace by hand, which breaks V5 ("keeps every attempt") and V7 (all answer files committed). Nothing says whether a void counts toward R7's two attempts. The script counts an "other" declaration as a failed R7 attempt (check 8), while check 5 calls it a void that is re-run. Gemini agents often read a file with a terminal command, which is itself grounds for a void, so this will come up often. How it is handled decides which packets end up with a V4 code.

findings.title: Answers with duplicate JSON keys are recorded as valid, with the last value silently kept
findings.problem: parse_answer uses plain json.loads, which keeps the last value of a repeated key. An answer that gives both labels for one item is stored as valid with whichever label came last. A repeated top-level "answers" key also hides a malformed first list. The same applies to case records, for example two "class" keys.
findings.evidence: 23-am1-v4.py:327 `return json.loads(text), bool(fence)`. Reproduction: audit-04 with every entry written as `{"id": "...", "carries": true, "carries": false}` -> "audit-04.attempt-1.json: valid", and every stored carries is False; audit-05 with `{"answers": [{"id": "junk", "carries": 7}], "answers": [...]}` -> "audit-05.attempt-1.json: valid".

An agent that answers only in the chat leaves no answer.json, and collect --workspace then ends in a FileNotFoundError traceback with no attempt stored. The fallback, --response, skips the workspace check, and its record carries the same channel string with no field saying the answer came from a file the author made. Whether a chat-only answer counts as a failed attempt, a void or a collectable answer is not defined.

findings.title: Void answers can be discarded and re-asked without trace, and the author may know their own codes when doing so

With an unpinned model whose sampling settings are not exposed, each re-ask gives a new draw. So the operator can select V4's codes. findings.title: The copy-check trigger cannot be decided, and it chooses which kappa gates design-limit claims
findings.problem: Several parts of the trigger are undefined. The measure of 'agreement' is not named (kappa or percent agreement; eight labels or binary). The template says the copy check compares 'the whole record'. 'Clearly above' has no threshold, and 'the author's' does not say which of the two author agreements. The trigger matters: it switches the 0.40 rule from the author-V4 kappa to the lower of two. It would be decided after the kappas are known, so the author could steer whether a design-limit claim is allowed. That is what line 14 rules out. The check is also not diagnostic. Both models run the same 60k-character prompt with its procedural glosses, so model-model agreement above author-model agreement is expected from the shared instrument alone; it does not show model bias. Finally, the pre-codes have only blind codes, so 'whichever has the lower bound' is undefined for the final kappa.

findings.problem: The bound rule counts coder disagreement on implementation versus not as unclear (lines 361, 453).
